name: Clawdbot / OpenClaw
description: Self-hosted personal AI assistant gateway. Single long-running process owns all channel connections (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, iMessage, Matrix, Teams, 20+ others) and manages a WebSocket control plane at port 18789. Browser-based Control UI on the same port. Launched as Clawdbot Nov 2025, renamed Moltbot Jan 27 2026 (Anthropic trademark), renamed OpenClaw Jan 30 2026. 381k+ GitHub stars as of Apr 2026.
auth_default_note: Gateway auth token is generated during onboarding for loopback access, but no auth enforcement exists on the Control UI when exposed publicly. http.title:"Clawdbot Control" + http.status:200 = 1,770 hits with ZERO HTTP 401s across the entire exposed population. The UI is a local admin dashboard designed for loopback — public exposure is accidental but extremely common.
auth_config_env_note: CLAWDBOT_* and MOLTBOT_* legacy prefixes silently ignored as of 2026 rename. gateway.auth.token and gateway.auth.password are the openclaw.json config keys. remote.token/remote.password govern remote-client auth separately.
install_tell: npm install -g openclaw@latest && openclaw onboard --install-daemon; Docker: ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest on port 18789; config at ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json; daemon via launchd (macOS) or systemd user service (Linux); Node 24 or Node 22.19+ required.
misconfig_patterns: Gateway bound to 0.0.0.0 without OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN/PASSWORD set
dmPolicy=open combined with exec tool access — any inbound DM triggers agent tool invocation
allowFrom misconfigured as string instead of numeric ID (Telegram) — allowlist silently bypassed (GitHub issue #57888)
Config validation failure drops security settings to empty config {} — resets dmPolicy to insecure default (GitHub issue #5052)
tools.exec.host=gateway (bypasses Docker sandbox, runs exec on host directly)
exec.approvals.set=off (disables confirmation gates on shell exec)
Reverse proxy strips auth headers — gateway sees unauthenticated WS from trusted proxy
Docker volume mounts with wrong UID — container writes credentials world-readable
security=full + ask=off combination (intentional default for trusted setups, dangerous when publicly exposed)
tool_integrations: Shell (exec tool — arbitrary OS command execution on host or sandboxed)

active_probe.false_positive_check: Verify page contains a gateway management UI element (session list, channel status, config tab) not just a string match. Check /healthz returns 200 with JSON body as secondary confirmation.

shodan_dorks.combined: http.title:"OpenClaw" OR http.title:"Clawdbot Control" OR http.title:"Moltbot Control"

shodan_population.auth_status: ZERO HTTP 401s across 1,770 http.title:"Clawdbot Control" http.status:200 population

deployment_tells: npm global install: which openclaw returns /usr/local/bin/openclaw or ~/.nvm/versions/node/.../bin/openclaw
systemd user service at ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw.service (Linux daemon install)
Docker: ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest image; compose project name openclaw
State dir: ~/.openclaw/ contains credentials/, agents/, sessions/, secrets.json
Process: node process named openclaw-gateway or openclaw with gateway subcommand
Railway, Zeabur, Vercel AI Gateway, Hostinger one-click deploy templates publicly documented
pivot_paths: /api/channels/ — enumerate connected channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack etc)
/api/v1/admin/rpc config.get — full config dump including channel tokens and API key refs
~/.openclaw/credentials/ — channel bot tokens (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp)
node.invoke RPC — arbitrary tool invocation including exec on host

vulnerabilities.name: OpenClaw Auth Token Exfiltration via gatewayUrl leading to 1-Click RCE
vulnerabilities.description: Control UI auto-trusts user-supplied gatewayUrl query param, opens WebSocket to attacker-controlled host, sends stored auth token. No WebSocket origin header validation. Attacker replays token, calls node.invoke to run arbitrary shell commands. Attack chain: exec.approvals.set=off disables confirmation, tools.exec.host=gateway escapes Docker sandbox.
vulnerabilities.patch_description: Gateway URL confirmation modal requiring explicit user approval before connecting to new gateway URLs

vulnerabilities.name: Config validation failure silently resets security settings to insecure defaults
vulnerabilities.description: When loadConfig() fails validation (e.g. missing plugin manifests), returns empty config {} instead of erroring, silently resetting dmPolicy, allowFrom allowlist, and auth settings.
vulnerabilities.status: CANDIDATE - no CVE assigned as of 2026-06-26

vulnerabilities.name: Telegram allowFrom numeric ID mismatch allows allowlist bypass
vulnerabilities.description: openclaw configure writes Telegram allowFrom as string type, but DM allowlist matching requires numeric IDs. Allowlist silently bypassed for all Telegram DMs.
vulnerabilities.status: CANDIDATE - no CVE assigned as of 2026-06-26

auth_evidence: Population survey: http.title:"Clawdbot Control" http.status:200 = 1,770 hits, ZERO HTTP 401s across the entire population. Gateway default port 18789 shows 166 hits. Gateway docs state Control UI is local-only (http://127.0.0.1:18789) but public exposure is common via 0.0.0.0 bind, reverse proxy misconfiguration, or cloud one-click deploys. CrowdStrike found 42,000+ exposed instances with 93.4% auth bypass rate. Censys found 21,000+ over plain HTTP at CVE-2026-25253 disclosure. Tool integrations include shell exec (host or Docker sandbox), browser, email (Gmail Pub/Sub), calendar, cron. Largest confirmed unauth agent framework population on the internet.
sensitive_assets: LLM provider API keys (billed to operator per request) — in auth-profiles.json
Shell exec access to host OS via exec tool (no sandbox by default for main session)
Channel bot credentials (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage tokens)
Email (Gmail Pub/Sub) and calendar integrations if configured
Browser sessions via browser automation tool
Session transcripts stored in ~/.openclaw/ readable by any local process
severity_note: Unauth access = shell exec on host via node.invoke + exec tool, LLM API key theft (operator-billed), full channel bot token exfiltration, email/calendar access. CVE-2026-25253 enables 1-click RCE from a single malicious URL click even when auth is configured. Largest unauth agent framework population on the internet.
